finding: five of the six axes previously read the SAME scalar — scene-linear peak divided by median — from five regions. Those are transformations of one quantity, not five independent axes, and every one of them describes how TALL a highlight is. What separates a matte from a satin is how WIDE it is.
correction: each region axis now reports its own lobe width, measured on its own surface. Height remains represented once, by HIGHLIGHT_PEAK.

HIGHLIGHT_FWHM.formula: fraction of region samples above the half-height between median and p99.9

HIGHLIGHT_PEAK.formula: scene-linear p99.9, normalised by the frame median

SPECULAR_TO_DIFFUSE_RATIO.depends_on: shares its numerator with HIGHLIGHT_PEAK — retained because the denominator differs, but NOT counted as independent of it when both clear

SHEEN_REGION_RESPONSE.physical: lobe width on a shallow curve

independence_basis: the three clearing axes are measured on three DIFFERENT physical surfaces — a convex quarter-cylinder, a 74-degree grazing ramp and a 1.6 mm bevel — so they are not transformations of one scalar
